name: tstmd-network-connectivity
title: Crosslinking builds ECM network connectivity (real TST-MD, 2D)
question: In the real 2D bead-spring ECM engine, does increasing the number of crosslinks raise the connectivity (giant component) of the fiber network, reproducing the percolation mechanism that underlies Fig 2B of Keijzer & Merks 2026?
hypothesis: With no crosslinks the fiber network is essentially disconnected; adding crosslinks sharply raises the fraction of beads in the largest connected component, a percolation-onset signature.
objective: Sweep the requested crosslink count over {0, 500, 2000, 5000, 10000, 20000} through the real engine and measure, from the built network, the giant-component fraction (beads nodes; fiber bonds + crosslinks edges).
description: REAL output of the TST-MD engine via the viva-tstmd Docker bridge. For each crosslink setting a fresh crosslinked network (1500 strands) is generated and its giant-component fraction measured. NOTE: requested != created — only bead pairs within crosslink_max_r=6 are linked, so created counts are {0, 397, 1661, 3754, 7212, 13231}. A 2D, mechanism-level analog of the percolation result in Keijzer & Merks 2026 Fig 2B.

readouts.name: Giant-component fraction
readouts.description: Size of the largest connected component (beads = nodes, bonds+crosslinks = edges) / number of beads.

readouts.name: Crosslinks created
readouts.description: Crosslink bonds actually formed (bond type != fiber) for each requested count.

behavior_tests.name: Crosslinking connects the fiber network (percolation onset)
behavior_tests.description: Introducing crosslinks raises the giant component by more than 10x over the uncrosslinked network. Measured: giant component 0.0007 (0 crosslinks) -> 0.177 (397 created) -> ~0.29 (>=1661 created) — a >250x jump at onset.
behavior_tests.pass_if: giant_component at the lowest nonzero crosslink setting >= 10 * giant_component at zero crosslinks
behavior_tests.paper_reference: Keijzer & Merks 2026, Fig 2B (network percolation / giant component rises with crosslinking)

evidence.from_test: Crosslinking connects the fiber network (percolation onset)

findings.statement: Crosslinking sharply raises ECM network connectivity: the giant component jumps from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) to 0.18 at ~400 crosslinks and ~0.29 at >=1600 — the percolation-onset mechanism behind Fig 2B.

Connectivity saturates near 0.29 at these reduced fiber/crosslink densities rather than reaching full percolation (~1.0 at the paper's HPC scale). The ONSET direction is reproduced; the full percolated regime needs near-paper-scale networks (a documented scope/calibration limit).

conclusion: The real engine reproduces, in 2D, the percolation-onset mechanism of Fig 2B: crosslinking takes the fiber network from disconnected to a connected cluster. Full percolation (giant component ~1.0) is not reached at the reduced CPU densities used — a documented scope limit, not a claimed match.
key_assumptions: Giant component measured on the built network (it is a network property, roughly constant over the run).
Reduced densities vs paper HPC scale; 1 seed per crosslink setting.
requested crosslinks != created (crosslink_max_r=6 gating); the created count is the honest x-axis.
